title: launcher.json
description: A built app's settings list (dm/launcher.json in an IPA's app, Contents/Resources/dm/launcher.json in a Mac app), written by dm/games/settings.py from dm/games/settings.tsv. docs/frontends.md describes the fields. Schema 1 grows only by optional fields: a reader ignores fields it does not know, and a field keeps its meaning.

schema.description: The list's version; a list without it is schema 1 written before the field existed.

console.description: The console the game was built for: 'switch2' when its sdk module was built for the Switch 2, else 'switch1'. A front end may show it (the launcher's line under the game's name); a list without it says nothing about the console.

term.description: <VAR>=<v>/<v> or <VAR>!=<v>/<v> (another row's current value, a range compared as a number, or the environment for a switch no row sets; false when neither has the variable), or a device term: device:<iphone/ipad/mac>, screen<r, screen>=r, window<r, window>=r, hz<n, hz>=n, haptics:none, controller:none, tv:none, mfx:none, capture:on. A term a reader does not know is false.

option.description: The value the row shows while the terms hold, one it takes.

when.description: Terms that must all hold: the same as one of the row's whole-row inactive rules.

option.description: choice or toggle: the value the rule is about; without it, the whole row.

why.description: The reason, one short line, shown as the row's note (and beside an option a rule names).

env.description: The environment switch the setting sets.

section.description: The heading it goes under (Game, Controls and Performance today); sections and rows come in the order to show them. A reader draws a section it does not know like the others, under its name.

note.description: The line under the label; empty for most settings.

default.description: The tested default for this app's platform, with profile defaults resolved.

on.description: toggle: the value the switch takes when on.

off.description: toggle: the value the switch takes when off.

base.description: Render scale only: the 3D views' size the scale multiplies, docked and handheld, from the game's profile; absent for most games.

level.description: basic: a setting a front end shows first. Without it, the front end decides.

needs.description: <VAR>=<value>: a sub-setting, drawn only while the row that sets <VAR> has that value. A row naming a variable this list does not have stays drawn.

inactive.description: The row, or with option one of its options, is drawn greyed (not selectable) with why as its note while a rule's terms all hold: another setting or the device makes it do nothing. Its saved value stays as it is.

hint.description: The row, or with option one of its options, stays selectable and shows why as its note while a rule's terms all hold: it does something only in some situations.

hide.description: The row is not drawn while one entry's terms all hold: device terms only, for a setting that can never do anything on this device. Its saved value stays as it is.

shows.description: While an entry's terms all hold (the row is then greyed by its whole-row inactive rule with the same terms), the row shows option, the value the host uses then, instead of the saved choice; the saved value stays as it is and is shown again when the terms stop holding. A reader that does not know the field shows the saved choice.

preset.description: The value the row takes in each launcher preset besides Balanced (the defaults): battery and quality, each a value the row takes (its default where the preset leaves the row as tested). A front end applies a preset to the rows that have one, except rows an env file or the launch sets and rows or options a rule greys; a preset whose values all match is the one shown as chosen. A reader ignores presets it does not know.
